# EXP-018: route warping is not a reliable gait-placement lever (2026-09-01)

The route-warped pilot (`docs/ramp-e1-route-warped-protocol.md`) ran from clean commit
`d5e53c4` and stopped at Stage B with a harness defect, after producing its **Stage-A
primary endpoint**. Evidence: `outputs/exp018_route_warped_stepover/` (failure schema
`exp018-route-warped-stepover-failure-v1`, stage `program_render`); 62 samples launched
and returned with exact accounting (8 donor + 48 pool + 6 warped, 0 arms).

## What passed

* **Donor determinism.** All eight donor clips regenerated byte-identically to exp017's
  archive, the selector re-chose seed 2603, and the freshly extracted packet payload
  reproduced the archived content hash exactly. The frozen-bundle reproduction gate works.
* **Pool eligibility 11/16** left-side seeds under the frozen v3 identities — inside the
  0.66–0.75 rate predicted from the calibration, and comfortably above the N=6 gate.

## Stage A: 1/6 persistence

Of the six selected seeds regenerated under their own outcome-free calibrated route warp,
**one** still placed a complete left swing at the obstacle within exp017's unchanged
±8-frame gate.

| seed | stratum | linear apex | warped outcome |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 3800 | fast | 108 | **persists**: apex 99, shift +7, spatial error −14.5 mm |
| 3801 | fast | 92 | single cycle at apex 43 → shift +49 |
| 3803 | fast | 90 | cycles at 52/72/142/179 → best shift +17 |
| 3804 | fast | 88 | single cycle at apex 171 → shift −85 |
| 3805 | slow | 103 | no complete left swing at all |
| 3808 | slow | 110 | no complete left swing at all |

All six warped clips tracked their prescribed route well (progress ratios 0.996–1.003), so
this is not a route-following failure. **The prior re-plans its gait when the root-path
timing changes**: the apex the program was built around is not where the swing lands after
re-conditioning, and two seeds lost swing structure entirely.

## Mechanism: a route-length coupling inherited from the calibration

The route program reparameterizes the fixed **7.2 m** pilot route, but the calibration
discovers cycles at three speeds whose routes are **4.776 / 7.200 / 9.552 m**. The
outcome-free minimum-deformation key measures deformation against the 7.2 m reference, so
it systematically selects cycles observed on a *different-length* route:

| seed | stratum | observed route | warped route | max Δspeed | max Δposition |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3800, 3801, 3803, 3804, 3810 | fast | 9.552 m | 7.200 m | ~0.34 m/s | **2.35 m** |
| 3805, 3808 | slow | 4.776 m | 7.200 m | ~0.31 m/s | **2.42 m** |

The "minimum-deformation" program is therefore a ~2.4 m displacement of the conditioning
relative to the route the cycle was actually observed under — not a small perturbation.
Only 1 of the 13 v3 validation selections used the reference stratum, so nearly every
selection is cross-length. This is a defect in the calibration's selection key, exposed
only because Stage A measured persistence before any packet arm existed. The staged design
worked as intended: no packet effect is confounded with this.

## Second defect: exp017's channel allowlist was dead code

Stage B aborted with `E1 writes unexpected ARDY channels: ['global_rot_data',
'root_pos']`. exp017's `ALLOWED_NONZERO_CHANNELS = {root_2d, root_y_pos,
global_joints_rots}` names **do not exist** in the model, whose `slice_dict` is
`{root_pos, global_root_heading, local_joints_positions, global_rot_data, velocities,
foot_contacts}`. The assertion's `missing = ALLOWED - usage` branch would have aborted
*any* real arm generation; it survived because exp017 never reached program rendering on a
real model (all three attempts failed earlier). Both halves of the guard are corrected to
the real names, preserving the original intent: root position and global rotations
constrained, joint positions and body heading free.

## Consequence: the placement lever changes, and E1 is unblocked

Route warping is a weak lever for putting a gait event at a chosen scene position, and
this pilot cannot be rescued by widening the shift bound or re-selecting seeds after seeing
the outcome. The alternative lever is to choose the obstacle to match the gait rather than
warping the gait to match the obstacle — placing the obstacle at the nominal's own
apex progress on its **own generating route**, which makes the required shift zero by
construction and needs no regeneration at all.

Replayed on exp018's already-generated pool (frozen Pmin, packet window, left side, cycle
nearest mid-route), that lever yields **12/16 seeds** with a placeable obstacle at zero
warp (3 slow, 3 reference, 6 fast; obstacle x from 1.04 m to 5.03 m). exp019
(`docs/ramp-e1-gait-matched-protocol.md`) uses it to run the paired representation
comparison E1 has been blocked on since exp017, adding the unmodified nominal as a free
third reference arm. Its scope is explicitly narrower: per-seed placement supports the
paired absolute-vs-residual comparison, and supports no fixed-scene planning claim.
